summary: The text presents a variety of arguments against various aspects of E-Rate, including parental opt-out rights, restrictions on screen time, and requirements for independent research verification of tech. It also mentions the need for parental oversight and the prohibition of certain forms of social media for students.

claims.argument: Screen-time limits could increase costs for schools
claims.evidence_quote:
- K-12 parents should have the right to opt-out of school-mandated tech, 
- Parents should have the right to opt-out of any AI use,
- Parents should have the right to opt-out of 1:1 device use (chromebooks, iPads, laptops, tablets),
- Student internet access should be allow-list only, 
- All forms of tech should be independent research verified,
